answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance cannot rely on one account equalling one vote, because identities are cheap to copy. Stronger designs therefore price identity: staking collateral that is slashed on fraud, proof of sustained useful work that cannot be faked in bulk, and reputation that accrues slowly but is lost instantly. An attacker who wants many fake agents must then pay repeatedly, in stake, compute, and time, while honest agents reuse one verified history across tasks.
